title: Playbook walkthrough & KMS residency sync - Stonebridge Health
summary: Walkthrough of incident response playbook and KMS residency options focused on meeting Stonebridge Health RTO/RPO and data residency constraints. Covered SOC2 evidence, SSO/RBAC integration, audit log retention, proposed SLA thresholds, and oncall/escalation flows. Agreed next steps: share security pack, schedule tabletop, and pilot a dedicated KMS-residency setup.
action_items: Alex Chen | Share full Security Pack (SOC 2 report, ISO gap doc, audit log schema) | 2026-08-04
Priya Kapoor | Schedule 90-minute incident tabletop with SRE + compliance | 2026-08-10
Benji O'Neil | Provide network diagram and current KMS vendor details | 2026-08-06
Marta Reyes | Confirm RTO/RPO acceptance criteria and escalation contacts | 2026-08-07
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2/ISO artifacts link: https://redwood.example/security-pack/stb-49372
Schedule tabletop (Priya to own) and invite SRE, oncall manager, compliance
Customer to review KMS residency options and confirm if HSM/KMS integration with customer-managed keys required
Plan a short pilot of dedicated capacity with prefix caching + KMS residency for a critical workload
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-01 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE); Marta Reyes (Stonebridge CISO); Benji O'Neil (Stonebridge Head of Platform); Sofia Tan (Stonebridge Compliance)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the, uh, account lead for Stonebridge. Priya my solutions engineer is with me. How's everyone?
[00:08] Marta Reyes: Hi Alex, thanks, yeah, thanks for setting this up, we've got Benji and Sofia on. Want to focus today on incident readiness and, erm, K M S residency questions.
[00:15] Priya Kapoor: Great, yeah so agenda — quick SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), then RTO/RPO and the escalation playbook.
[00:23] Benji O'Neil: Quick note — we are constrained by data residency, all PHI must stay in region-us-east-2, and our corporate KMS is HashiCorp Vault on prem. We need to understand connectivity options and whether Redwood Private can keep keys in our VPC.
[00:38] Alex Chen: Yep, understood. So on Redwood Private we support bring-your-own-KMS via KMS proxy and HSM integrations; sometimes the docs say "Redwood Privatee" in an old note, apologies for typos. We also have Dedicated capacity with customer KMS options but there are trade-offs.
[00:50] Sofia Tan: Also, audit logs — retention and tamper-evidence. Our compliance team needs seven years of immutable logs for certain flows.
[00:58] Priya Kapoor: On audit logs we can stream structured audit events to your S3 or into your SIEM via secure connector; retention and immutability depend on backend — if you put them into your S3 with object lock you get WORM behaviour. We also store a hashed copy in our append-only log for a limited retention if you opt in.
[01:16] Marta Reyes: Can you confirm encryption-in-transit and at-rest with customer keys? We need envelope encryption with customer KMS as the root.
[01:24] Alex Chen: Yes, envelope encryption is supported. The model weights and ephemeral caches are encrypted at rest; the root key can be your Vault. We use an internal keystore but can wrap with your root via KMS API. There have been a couple of earlier mislabels in our docs where they wrote KV cache as K V cache incorrectly in the pdf, but the flow is standard.
[01:41] Speaker 2: Uh hm.
[01:45] Benji O'Neil: On RTO/RPO — our target is RTO 15 minutes for critical inference endpoints, RPO 1 hour for customer-facing apps. How feasible is that across hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[01:55] Priya Kapoor: Hosted API is tricky for 15-minute RTO if you need customer-managed keys and cross-region failover. For Dedicated or Private we can design active-active with warm standby in a second region; typical config to hit 15 minutes RTO is warm standby plus automated DNS failover and pre-warmed KV caches. RPO depends on how you persist KV cache and prompt history; if you rely on persistent request logs to reconstruct, we can get to ~1 hour RPO. Hosted, you'd be looking at higher RPO unless you add custom replication.
[02:19] Marta Reyes: So sounds like Private with BYOK is the direction. What's the SLA we can expect? We have 99.95% as our internal bar.
[02:27] Alex Chen: Our Dedicated SLA can be 99.95% with reserved capacity contracts; Private SLA depends on deployment (on-prem SLA is customer+Redwood ops blended). We typically see 99.9 to 99.99 depending on topology. For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated with cross-region failover to meet your bar.
[02:44] Sofia Tan: Escalation: in an incident we want a clear path — who pagers, who owns incident commander, and when legal/compliance is looped in. Can you walk through Redwood's typical escalation ladder?
[02:56] Priya Kapoor: Sure. Normal severe incident flow: 1) Monitoring triggers alert -> Pager duty to SRE oncall (first 15 mins). 2) If not resolved in 15-30 mins, escalate to SE and AE; AE (Alex) will notify customer success and open a Jira Sev1 runbook. 3) If customer data exposure suspected, we escalate to legal/compliance and schedule a call within 60 mins. 4) We have an SLA-specific timeline for RTO notifications and status cadence. We can adapt the playbook to include your legal contact Marta and your oncall rotations.
[03:21] Benji O'Neil: Any examples of RTO postmortems? We need runbook samples with the primary/secondary ops contact, templates for communication, and a playbook for rollback to previous model versions.
[03:31] Alex Chen: We'll share a redacted postmortem and a runbook template. Also, functionally we support automatic fallback to a smaller, lower-cost variant if GPU pools are overloaded, that helps keep latency SLOs while you operate in degraded mode. One caveat, sometimes the auto-fallback name in logs is truncated and looks like "rmw-fallback" — small doc glitch.
[03:50] Marta Reyes: For compliance, how do you handle evidence for SOC2? Access logs, config change records, SSO events, key rotations?
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: SOC2 artifact pack includes access logs, config change audit trail, KMS rotation schedule, SSO token issuance logs (SAML/Okta), RBAC changes. We'll provide a mapping spreadsheet that maps each control to where the evidence lives. Note: sometimes token events get labeled "authn" in our export; we'll annotate these.
[04:18] Sofia Tan: We need RBAC integration with our SCIM/Okta and role sync, plus support for attribute-based access for data-scoped roles.
[04:26] Priya Kapoor: We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. Attribute-based access is available but needs SAML assertions mapping; we can show an example claim mapping during the tabletop.
[04:36] Speaker 3: (mumble)
[04:38] Benji O'Neil: Network specifics — we'll provide the VPC peering model, but if you're doing private deployment behind a customer firewall, what do you need?
[04:45] Alex Chen: For VPC/private we typically use a customer-controlled NAT + interface endpoints. For on-prem we use an agent-based reverse-tunnel for control-plane calls so there's no inbound opening. We'll share the network checklist.
[04:58] Marta Reyes: Back to RTO/RPO — can you guarantee RPO of one hour if we use persistent backing store for conversation history?
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: Yes if you persist to your S3 or DB and we replicate at write-time to a secondary region, we can achieve ~1 hour or better. If you rely solely on in-memory KV cache, the RPO will be longer unless you checkpoint frequently. We'll recommend checkpointing every 10 minutes for critical flows.
[05:24] Alex Chen: Quick note on cost trade-offs — more frequent checkpointing and cross-region replication increases egress and storage costs; we'll model that in a pilot.
[05:33] Sofia Tan: About the tabletop — we want scenario: data-plane latency spike, potential key compromise, and partial region outage.
[05:41] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. We can simulate the key compromise run: steps to revoke keys, rotate, switch to backup key, and how to validate custody. We'll also exercise the communication cadence.
[05:52] Benji O'Neil: Who's oncall from Redwood in the first 60 mins? We need names and phone/pager details for our roster.
[05:59] Alex Chen: We'll provide the oncall matrix. Typically first responder is SRE oncall (name varies by timezone), then SE (Priya) and AE (me). We'll add a direct escalation to SRE lead for severity two and above.
[06:13] Marta Reyes: Regarding audit log retention — can we request immutable storage with legal hold for specific timeframes?
[06:18] Priya Kapoor: You can if you put the logs in your own object store with lock/hold; Redwood can also sign and store hash anchors for tamper-evidence. We'll show the flow in the artifacts.
[06:30] Speaker 1: (laughs) yeah
[06:34] Alex Chen: Ok, I'll recap and then we can assign next steps. Recap: 1) Customer leaning to Private with BYOK and warm standby for RTO 15m/RPO 1h; 2) Need network diagram, KMS vendor detail; 3) Redwood to share SOC2/ISO artifact pack and runbook templates; 4) Schedule tabletop.
[06:52] Marta Reyes: That matches our expectations. Couple of clarifying Qs — for pilot, can we scope a single critical endpoint only and keep others on hosted?
[07:01] Priya Kapoor: Yes, you can pilot a single endpoint on Dedicated/Private while leaving the rest on Hosted; routing is policy driven so it's straightforward. We'll also show cost delta.
[07:12] Benji O'Neil: For the KMS integration, do you support Vault transit engine or do we need to expose KMS API?
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: We have a vault adapter for transit engine; sometimes infra teams prefer a proxy that talks to Vault's API. We'll work with your Vault admin — Benji — on the exact approach.
[07:32] Sofia Tan: One more thing — log correlation IDs must be present in every response to tie back to PII redaction flows. Is that automatic?
[07:40] Alex Chen: Correlation IDs are emitted at request time and can be propagated; we also can mask PII at the ingestion layer if you enable the redaction pipeline. Note the redaction is best-effort and flaggable for review.
[07:53] Speaker 2: mmhmm
[08:00] Marta Reyes: Ok, next steps and deadlines please.
[08:03] Alex Chen: Action items captured, we'll send the security pack by Wednesday 2026-08-04, Priya will send a tabletop invite for week of Aug 10. Benji will share network diagrams and Vault details by Aug 6. Marta will confirm escalation contacts.
[08:18] Benji O'Neil: Sounds good.
[08:20] Sofia Tan: Thanks everyone.
[08:22] Alex Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:24] Transcript note: Minor transcription errors present; names and acronyms occasionally misrecognized (e.g., "K M S" vs KMS, "rmw-fallback" log tag).
